name: No order to follow
problem: People who want to apply ESOI have the five record types and the principles but no order to follow. They do not know what to do first, write implementations before deciding what best means, trust a metric before checking that it tells good from bad, skip the perspectives that would find gaps, and stop after the first build instead of looping back.
who_has_it: Anyone applying ESOI to a project, product, course, process or code for the first time, the AI agents asked to apply it, and people who apply it often but skip steps under time pressure.
why_it_matters: The records only optimize an intent when they are made in an order that decides best before building and keeps measuring after; without an order, ESOI is applied partially and the parts that address the biggest risks are the ones skipped.
why_hard: The work is a network, not a line, so any order is a simplification; small tasks and large projects need very different depth; and the order has to change as ESOI itself changes.
existing_attempts: The 2020 Project Documentation board checklist (an order, but without metric checks, interfaces, the split test, perspectives or retirement); the one-hour guide in this repository (a short pass, no full order); general project-management and design-thinking processes, which do not compare implementations by metric.
